### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A03 was executed exactly once in every trace (200 of 200) and sat at the very start of traces (median relative position 0); in the later window it is not observed at all (0 of 200). [OCC001, POS002]
- A07 shows the mirror image: not observed earlier, it runs exactly once in every trace in the later window, at a stable position about three quarters into the trace. [OCC002, POS004]
- Routing changed at both ends of the trace. Earlier, A03's outgoing transitions led to A02 in about 86 in 100 cases, with small shares to A06 (about 6 in 100), A05 (about 5 in 100), A04 (about 2 in 100) and A01 (about 1 in 100); in the later window A03 has no observed outgoing transitions. A04, which earlier led to A01 in about 99 in 100 cases, now leads to A07 in every case, and A07 leads to A01 in every case. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- A02 now opens the traces (median relative position 0.25 earlier, 0 in the later window) and A04 sits earlier (median 0.75 earlier, 0.5 in the later window). [POS001, POS003]
- Co-occurrence with A03 flipped to separation: earlier, A03 appeared together with A01, A02 and A04 in every trace and preceded them (before A01 in about 199 of 200 traces, before A02 in about 86 in 100, before A04 in about 99 in 100); in the later window A01, A02 and A04 always appear without A03. A07 now co-occurs with A01, A02 and A04 in every trace, always after A02 and A04 and before A01. [REL001, REL003, REL005, REL006, REL002, REL004, REL007]
- Distances shifted at the end of the trace: A04 reached A01 in one step in about 99 in 100 traces earlier and now takes two steps, with A07 in between, in all traces; A02 reached A01 in three steps in about 87 in 100 traces earlier and now needs four steps in all traces; the A02→A04 distance stayed at two steps (about 88 in 100 earlier, all traces in the later window). [LAG003, LAG001, LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural restructuring involving A03, A02, A04, A07 and A01: in the later window, A03 — previously a mandatory opening activity that passed control to A02 in about 86 in 100 cases — is no longer executed, traces begin with A02, and a new mandatory activity A07 runs between A04 and A01, so the earlier shape A03 → A02 → … → A04 → A01 appears as A02 → … → A04 → A07 → A01. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS003, POS004, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL007, LAG001, LAG003]

The screening qualified 19 control-flow items against roughly 0.13 expected if nothing had changed, so chance sampling cannot account for the ensemble; the change is shown directly by successor, relation, position and distance evidence, all items point to the same restructuring, and the middle segment A02 → A04 (two steps apart) is unchanged between the windows. [DIR002, DIR003, REL004, REL007, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: the evidence cannot establish whether dropping A03 and inserting A07 were one coordinated redesign or two independent changes, and A03's zero participation only shows it was not observed in the later window; the evidence also says nothing about A05 and A06 or about the activity sitting between A02 and A04, which it does not identify. [OCC001, DIR001]

Other differences: earlier, about 14 in 100 traces routed A03 to a continuation other than A02 (A05 about 5 in 100, A06 about 6 in 100), and about 13 in 100 traces showed a three-step A02→A04 distance; neither is observed in the later window, where A02→A04 is always two steps. [DIR001, LAG002]

- Screening: 26 units tested, 19 items qualified, 0.13 expected without change (control_flow family only). 19 items vs 0.13 expected — vastly more than chance. So the count comparison passes: this is not what an unchanged process produces.

Now let me reconstruct the process behaviour from the evidence.

Activities mentioned: A01, A02, A03, A04, A05, A06, A07.

Before window:
- OCC001: A03 present in 100% of traces (mean 1.0 per trace, participation 1.0). After: 0%.
- OCC002: A07 absent before (0%), present in 100% after (mean 1.0).
- DIR001: A03's outgoing transitions before: A02 (86%), A06 (5.5%), A05 (5%), A04 (2%), A01 (1%). After: empty (A03 not observed).
- DIR002: A04's outgoing before: A01 (99%), A03 (1%). After: A07 (100%).
- DIR003: A07's outgoing before: empty. After: A01 (100%).
- POS001: A02 position: before mean 0.215 (median 0.25), after mean 0.0 (median 0). So A02 moved from around position 0.25 to position 0 (start).
- POS002: A03 position: before mean ~0.049 (median 0), after absent.
- POS003: A04 position: before mean 0.746 (median 0.75), after mean 0.5 (median 0.5).
- POS004: A07 position: before absent, after mean 0.75 (median 0.75).
- REL001 (A01, A03): before co-occur 100%, B_before_A (A03 before A01) 99.5%. After: A_only 100% (A01 present, A03 absent).
- REL002 (A01, A07): before A_only 100% (A01 present, A07 absent). After: co-occurrence 100%, B_before_A (A07 before A01) 100%.
- REL003 (A02, A03): before co-occur 100%, B_before_A (A03 before A02) 86%, A_before_B 14%. After: A_only 100% (A02 present, A03 absent).
- REL004 (A02, A07): before A_only 100%. After: co-occurrence 100%, A_before_B (A02 before A07) 100%.
- REL005 (A03, A04): before co-occur 100%, A_before_B (A03 before A04) 98.5%. After: B_only 100% (A04 present, A03 absent).
- REL006 (A03, A07): before A_only 100% (A03 present, A07 absent). After: B_only 100% (A07 present, A03 absent).
- REL007 (A04, A07): before A_only 100%. After: co-occurrence 100%, A_before_B (A04 before A07) 100%.
- LAG001 (A02 → A01): before gap 3 (86.5%) or 4 (13.5%); after gap 4 (100%).

- LAG003 (A04 → A01): before gap 1 (99%); after gap 2 (100%).

Let me reconstruct the before process:

Positions (normalized, presumably position / trace length or fraction): A02 at ~0.215 mean, median 0.25. A03 at ~0.049 mean, median 0. A04 at ~0.746 mean, median 0.75.

Hmm, positions are fractions of trace length presumably. Let me think about trace structure.

From REL: A03 before A02 (86%), A03 before A01 (99.5%), A03 before A04 (98.5%). A02 → A01 gap 3-4. A02 → A04 gap 2-3. A04 → A01 gap 1.

So before: A03 (near start, position ~0) → A02 (position ~0.25) → ... → A04 (position ~0.75) → A01 (end, gap 1 from A04).

Wait, A02 → A01 gap 3-4, A02 → A04 gap 2-3, A04 → A01 gap 1. So A02 ... (2-3 steps) ... A04, A01. That's consistent: A02 at position p, A04 at p+2 or p+3, A01 at p+3 or p+4.

A03's outgoing: mostly A02 (86%), also A06 (5.5%), A05 (5%), A04 (2%), A01 (1%). So A03 → A02 mostly.

A04's outgoing: A01 (99%), A03 (1%). So A04 → A01.

What about A05, A06? They appear as successors of A03 in ~5% of cases each. No other evidence about them. They're minor.

So before structure roughly: A03 → A02 → (something) → A04 → A01, with A03 at the very start (median position 0), A02 at ~0.25, A04 at ~0.75, A01 at end.

Hmm, but positions are fractions. If trace length is 4 (A03, A02, A04, A01), positions 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1? A02 median 0.25 suggests length 4 with positions 0,1,2,3 normalized by (n-1)? Or normalized by length: 1/4 = 0.25. A04 median 0.75 = 3/4. A03 median 0. A01 would be at 1.0 presumably.

Actually LAG says A02 → A04 gap 2 or 3, A02 → A01 gap 3 or 4. So between A02 and A04 there's 1-2 events, and between A04 and A01 there's 0 events (adjacent, gap 1). So trace: A03, A02, ?, A04, A01 or A03, A02, A04, A01.

If trace = A03, A02, X, A04, A01 (5 events): A02 at 1, A04 at 3, A01 at 4. Normalized by 5: 0.2, 0.6, 0.8. Normalized by 4: 0.25, 0.75, 1.0. A02 median 0.25 ✓, A04 median 0.75 ✓. So traces have 5 events with one event X between A02 and A04 in some cases? But LAG A02→A04 gap 2 (87.5%) or 3 (12.5%). Gap 2 means one event between. Gap 3 means two events between.

Hmm, wait. Actually maybe there are variants. A03's outgoing: A02 86%, A06 5.5%, A05 5%, A04 2%, A01 1%. So in ~14% of traces, A03 leads to something else (A05, A06, A04, A01). And REL003: A03 before A02 in 86% — consistent. In the other 14%, A02 still occurs (participation 1.0) but not right after A03.

Hmm, but A02 participation is 1.0 before. And A02 → A01 gap 3 (86.5%) or 4 (13.5%). So in the 86% variant, A02→A01 gap 3: A02, X, A04, A01 — one event between A02 and A04? Wait gap 3 from A02 to A01: A02 at i, A01 at i+3. A04 at i+2 (gap 2 from A02). So A02, ?, A04, A01. What's the "?" event? Could be A05 or A06? But those only occur in ~5% each as A03's successor...

Hmm, wait. Maybe the "?" is another activity not in the evidence (evidence only covers units that qualified). The screening tested 26 units; only items that changed appear. So there could be other activities (A05, A06, and maybe others) that didn't change.

Actually, let me not over-reconstruct. The key point: I don't need the full model. Let me reconstruct the after process:

After:
- A03 absent (0%).
- A07 present 100%, at position ~0.75 median, mean 0.75.
- A02 at position 0 (median 0, mean 0). So A02 is now the first event.
- A04 at position 0.5 median.
- A04 → A07 (100% of A04's outgoing).
- A07 → A01 (100%).
- REL004: A02 before A07 (100%), co-occur.

Normalized by (5-1)=4: A02 at 0, A04 at 0.5, A07 at 0.75, A01 at 1.0. ✓ That matches! So positions are normalized by (length-1) presumably, or index/(n-1).

Check before with same normalization: trace A03, A02, X, A04, A01 (5 events): A03 at 0, A02 at 0.25, A04 at 0.75, A01 at 1.0. POS before: A02 median 0.25 ✓, A04 median 0.75 ✓, A03 median 0 ✓ (mean 0.049 — slightly above 0, maybe some variants where A03 is not first, e.g., A03 after something in the 14% variant... actually A03 mean 0.04875 with std 0.14, q75 = 0. So most at 0, some at higher positions).

Hmm wait, but before, what is X between A02 and A04? In after, X between A02 and A04 also exists (gap 2). Interesting — LAG002 before: gap 2 (87.5%), gap 3 (12.5%); after: gap 2 (100%). So the same intermediate event exists in both.

So the structural change: A03 (which was first, leading to A02 in 86% of cases) is removed, and A07 (which leads to A01) is added between A04 and A01. A02 now starts the trace.

Before: A03 → A02 → X → A04 → A01 (with variants where A03 → A05/A06/etc.)
After: A02 → X → A04 → A07 → A01

So A03 was replaced by... nothing at the start (A02 now first), and A07 inserted before A01. Alternatively: A03 removed from front, A07 added at end before A01.

Hmm, is this a "replacement of one path by another" or a "shift in path frequencies"? The guidance says: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows, and that only the shares between alternatives shift; it is not a replacement of one path by another. It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window..."

Here A03 goes from 100% to 0%, A07 from 0% to 100%. This is activity removal/addition — A03 became absent, A07 became mandatory. This is not a path-frequency shift; it's activities being removed/added (A03 removed, A07 added).

So the main hypothesis: the process changed such that A03 no longer occurs (it was a mandatory first activity before, occurring in all traces and typically leading to A02), and A07 was introduced as a new mandatory activity between A04 and A01. A02 now starts traces.

Supporting evidence:
- OCC001: A03 participation 100% → 0%.
- OCC002: A07 0% → 100%.
- DIR001: A03's outgoing transitions (mostly to A02) disappeared.
- DIR002: A04 now always leads to A07 (before: 99% to A01).
- DIR003: A07 always leads to A01.
- POS001: A02 moved from median position 0.25 to 0 (start).
- POS002: A03 gone.
- POS003: A04 from median 0.75 to 0.5.
- POS004: A07 appears at median 0.75.
- REL001, REL003, REL005, REL006: A03's relations with A01, A02, A04, A07 changed from co-occurrence to A01/A02/A04/A07-only.
- REL002, REL004, REL007: A07 now co-occurs with A01, A02, A04, in fixed orders (A07 before A01; A02 before A07; A04 before A07).

- LAG003: A04→A01 gap from 1 (99%, adjacent) to 2 (A07 between). ✓
- LAG002: A02→A04 gap mostly 2 in both (87.5% → 100%) — the middle part unchanged.

This is a coherent, consistent structural change: removal of A03 at the start and insertion of A07 between A04 and A01.

Screening: 19 items vs 0.13 expected — many times larger. So chance cannot explain the ensemble. Control-flow family only; no time or resource items. So I should not discuss time or resources.

Support level: The evidence directly and consistently shows the structural change. 19 items, all control-flow, all pointing to the same restructuring. Empirical strength 0.995 for all items (unusual for random splits). The count is ~146x the chance expectation. Direct relational evidence (DIR, REL, LAG) shows the change directly. I'd say "Supported hypothesis".

The hypothesis: A03 was removed from the process (previously a mandatory first step leading mostly to A02), and A07 was added as a new mandatory step between A04 and A01; A02 now begins traces. The middle segment A02 → (one event) → A04 remained unchanged.

Competing explanations: Could this be two separate changes (removal of A03 and addition of A07) rather than one? The evidence shows both, but whether they're one coordinated change or two is not determinable — but the hypothesis is about behaviour, and the evidence supports the structural description. A competing explanation: sampling — but 19 items vs 0.13 expected rules out chance as a whole. Another competing explanation: the traces in the after window come from a different variant of the process (e.g., a different path taken 100% of the time)... but A03 is completely absent and A07 completely present in all 200 traces each — that's a full replacement, not a path share shift. Could A03 be skipped conditionally? Participation 0 in 200 traces — it's not observed at all. Zero participation only means not observed.

Also note: the event X between A02 and A04 (gap 2) — we don't know what it is; it's unchanged. Also A05, A06 appear as A03 successors in ~5% each before; after A03 is gone, their status is unknown (no evidence). I shouldn't speculate much.

Now, one nuance: "A hypothesis about order or placement (an activity moved, activities swapped) needs relational or positional evidence (REL, LAG, POS, or successor changes in DIR) that shows that change directly." We have plenty: DIR002/DIR003 successor changes, REL002/REL004/REL007, LAG001/LAG003, POS001/POS003/POS004.

Main hypothesis statement: In the later window, A03 is no longer executed (before: in all traces, typically first, leading to A02 in about 86 in 100 cases), and A07 is executed in all traces between A04 and A01 (A04 now leads to A07 in all cases, A07 leads to A01 in all cases). Also LAG002: A02→A04 gap was 2 in ~88 in 100 before and 3 in ~13 in 100; after always 2 — a small consolidation. Hmm, that's part of the same picture. Also A02→A01 gap before: 3 in ~87 in 100, 4 in ~14 in 100; after always 4.

Actually the 14% variant before: A03 → A05/A06 (11%) etc. In those variants, what happens to A02? A02 participation is 1.0, and A02→A01 gap 4 in 13.5% of cases. So in the variant where A03 doesn't lead directly to A02, there's an extra event between A02 and A01. Possibly A03 → A05 → A02? We don't know. I shouldn't over-speculate. I can mention that before, A03's outgoing transitions also included A05 and A06 (about 5-6 in 100 each), which are no longer observed (since A03 is absent) — but careful: "An empty profile or an unobserved edge does not show that an activity or edge is absent from the process." A05 and A06 might still occur elsewhere; we just don't have evidence about them. I'll mention briefly that A03 previously also continued to A05/A06 in a minority of cases, and their fate is not covered by the evidence.

Let me also double check the "path frequency shift" condition doesn't apply: A03 absent in after window → doesn't apply. Correct, this is addition/removal.

Now the numbers, rounded:
- A03: participation 100% → 0% (200/200 → 0/200).
- A07: 0% → 100%.
- A03 → A02: about 86 in 100 of A03's outgoing transitions before.
- A04 → A01: about 99 in 100 before; A04 → A07: 100 in 100 after.
- A07 → A01: 100 in 100 after.

Structure of answer:

### Observed differences

Bullets:
1. A03 disappeared: before in all 200 traces (mean once per trace, typically first event, median position 0); after in 0 of 200. [OCC001, POS002]
2. A07 appeared: before 0 of 200; after in all 200 traces at median position 0.75. [OCC002, POS004]
3. Routing around the change: before, A03 led mostly to A02 (~86 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, with small shares to A06, A05, A04, A01); after A03 has no observed outgoing transitions. A04, which led to A01 in ~99 in 100 cases before, now leads to A07 in all cases; A07 in turn leads to A01 in all cases. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
4. A02 now starts traces: median position 0.25 → 0; A04 moved earlier: 0.75 → 0.5. [POS001, POS003]
5. Relations: before A03 co-occurred with A01, A02, A04 (and preceded them: A03 before A01 in ~100 in 100, before A02 in ~86 in 100, before A04 in ~99 in 100); after, A01, A02 and A04 appear without A03 in all traces. A07 now co-occurs with A01, A02, A04 in all traces, always after A02 and A04 and before A01. [REL001, REL003, REL005, REL006, REL002, REL004, REL007]
6. Gaps: A04→A01 was adjacent (~99 in 100) before, now 2 steps (A07 in between) in all; A02→A01 lengthened from 3 steps (~87 in 100) to 4 steps (all); A02→A04 unchanged at 2 steps (~88 in 100 before, all after). [LAG003, LAG001, LAG002]

Screening note: 19 control-flow items qualified vs ~0.13 expected without change. Maybe mention in inference instead. The observed differences section should be behavioural. I could add a line about the screening in inference.

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Hypothesis: a structural restructuring in which A03 was dropped from the start of the process and A07 was inserted between A04 and A01; A02 now opens traces. Before: A03 (first, in every trace) → A02 → ... → A04 → A01. After: A02 → ... → A04 → A07 → A01. The middle segment A02→A04 (two steps apart) is unchanged.
